svg.title: Features shared by all life and by all eukaryotes
svg.desc: An outer box lists features found in every living thing: DNA as genetic material, the same nearly universal genetic code, ribosomes, ATP as the energy carrier, glycolysis or close variants, and a plasma membrane. An inner box lists features found together only in eukaryotes: a nucleus with a double membrane, membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria, ER and Golgi, linear chromosomes, genes split by introns that are spliced out, and a cytoskeleton. The outer features were inherited from one ancestor of all life; the inner ones from a later ancestor of all eukaryotes.

g.text: • DNA as genetic material, copied before division
• ribosomes that translate mRNA into protein
• glycolysis or close variants of it
• a plasma membrane around the cell
• a nucleus with a double membrane
every group has all of the outer list,
so the outer features are older than
the split into the three domains.
Inner box: features found together only
in eukaryotes, inherited from a later
